header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Jordan Park (Redwood SE); Samir Patel (Redwood Infra) — Elena Ruiz (CascadeForge); Tom Nguyen (CascadeForge Platform Eng); Priya Sharma (CascadeForge Security); Ravi Desai (CascadeForge Product)
summary: Partner technical sync covering marketplace listing packaging, authentication patterns (OIDC/SAML/service accounts), private deployment prerequisites, and a focused streaming performance/kv-cache deep dive. Action items on both sides for staging access, benchmarks, and security artifacts.
topics: Marketplace listing manifest and packaging requirements
Auth patterns: SSO/SAML vs OIDC service accounts vs API keys for marketplace customers
Private deployment (VPC) onboarding checklist and IAM/KMS considerations
Streaming API behaviour and continuous batching/kv cache impacts
Performance benchmark plan and telemetry expectations
Next steps for pilot and compliance review
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call — we'll run through packaging, auth, and a deepdive into streaming performance.
[00:18] Elena (CascadeForge): hi all, excited to kick this off — we've got some marketplace timelines, hope we can align to Oct end for a soft listing.
[00:26] Jordan (Redwood SE): hi, yeah quick note, we typically need the listing manifest + container image or AMI with start scripts, and a small smoke test harness. We'll share a checklist.
[00:38] Tom (CascadeForge): got it, can you clarify the auth story for marketplace users — we expect both customer SSO and programmatic calls from our orchestration layer.
[00:47] Maya: yeah good question. For marketplace mode we support multiple patterns — SAML/SSO for UI users, and either short-lived OIDC tokens or service accounts for programmatic. We also have a private option where customers bind a VPC peering and use mutual-auth.
[01:05] Priya (CascadeForge Security): when you say mutual-auth, is that mTLS or is it IP-restriction plus IAM? We need KMS and HSM compatibility notes for our auditors.
[01:15] Samir (Redwood Infra): it's a mix depending on deployment. Our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS keys (HSM-backed) and can enforce mTLS between customer edge and the model runtime. In hosted we encrypt with our KMS but can integrate external KMS via grant.
[01:33] Ravi (CascadeForge Product): and what about data retention — logs, request/response retention in the marketplace listing? We have strict rules for customer data.
[01:43] Jordan: by default we retain minimal telemetry for billing and SLO monitoring; payloads are not retained beyond debug windows unless you opt-in. We'll send the data retention policy.
[01:55] Elena: ok good. Next, packaging — what's the expectation for the entrypoint? We use a custom runtime that wraps their inference calls.
[02:04] Maya: two options: publish a container image following our runtime contract (we'll share a template), or produce an AMI with init scripts if you're doing onprem/marketplace private listing. The manifest should include healthcheck endpoints, exposed ports, and a smoke test.
[02:22] Tom: do you require a particular logging format? We have JSON logs already but need to map fields for traceability.
[02:29] Jordan: JSON is ideal — if you emit request_id, model_id, and token_counts that's perfect. We'll add example parsers to the checklist.
[02:40] Maya: switching to streaming — Jordan will lead. Jordan?
[02:44] Jordan: yeah, streaming has two axes that matter: latency SLOs for first token, and throughput for sustained streams. Our runtime uses continuous batching and a KV cache which dramatically changes tail-latency for repeated prefixes.
[03:02] Tom: can you explain KV cache impact in lay terms? Our ops folks are skittish about cache correctness across versions.
[03:10] Jordan: sure, so KV cache stores key-value attention caches per session. If you have similar conversations, hit-rate goes up and token generation is faster. But if you pin rolling updates to model versions, we'll recommend a cache warmup strategy or fallback to a cold model to avoid staleness. Also note we do automatic cache invalidation on major model revs.
[03:33] Priya: is KV cache stored customer-side or in Redwood? From compliance we need to know who controls the keys.
[03:39] Samir: cache metadata is stored in our runtime but can be configured to use the customer's VPC storage when on Private. Keys for encryption can be customer KMS.
[03:49] Elena: that helps. Now on streaming perf — what's realistic for 100 concurrent streams with ~1.2k tokens per call?
[03:58] Jordan: depends on model and quantization. With our recommended quantized variant and batching, we can sustain ~6-8 fwd tokens/ms on A100-class nodes; for 100 concurrent streams you need autoscaling policies. We'll run a bench with your payload to give concrete numbers.
[04:16] Tom: what telemetry will you provide during the benchmark? We need per-request latencies, kv-cache hit rate, GPU utilization.
[04:23] Jordan: yes we'll surface token-level latency, per-route cost, histogram of tail latencies, and trace ids. We'll hand over the raw CSV/logs.
[04:34] Elena: excellent. On the marketplace listing page, we have a little policy: some of our customers require private tenancy. How do we show the options?
[04:42] Maya: listing metadata supports fields for deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), SLA tiers, and required integrations (KMS providers, SSO types). We'll give a sample listing page that you can review.
[04:55] Ravi: legal — is there a stub EULA we can start with? Our marketplace team will want to pre-clear it.
[05:01] Maya: yes we'll attach a standard marketplace EULA draft; you'll obviously want legal review.
[05:08] (crosstalk)
[05:12] Tom: diving into the private deployment checklist — network-wise what do you need? VPC peering? Transit gateway?
[05:18] Samir: we can support multiple network topologies. For AWS the most common is VPC peering with a dedicated routing table and a single NAT/edge. For high-throughput customers we recommend an AWS Transit Gateway to reduce routing complexity. We'll provide both templates.
[05:34] Priya: from security perspective: SAML SSO for UI, OIDC for programmatic ephemeral tokens, and service accounts with limited scopes. Is RBAC configurable?
[05:43] Jordan: yes RBAC at the token level, and enterprise customers can map their IdP groups to Redwood roles. We'll document the attribute mappings.
[05:52] Elena: ok great. Now the performance deepdive — Jordan please walk through the test plan we want to run with CascadeForge samples.
[05:58] Jordan: plan is: 1) smoke test with one stream for correctness; 2) ramp to 100 concurrent streams at your average token lengths; 3) run a steady 30-minute run and capture tail latency; 4) run a burst test to simulate sudden traffic; 5) repeat with cache cold/warm scenarios. We'll run both hosted (our shared infra) and a private deployment in your staging VPC.
[06:25] Tom: timeboxed — how long will you need to run the private test?
[06:29] Jordan: once you provide creds and VPC connectivity, we can stand up the infra in about 4 hours and run tests within the business day.
[06:36] Ravi: about cost, do you have a rough estimate for the test infra?
[06:40] Maya: we'll provide a test estimate; small flat fee to cover reserved nodes for the duration, but we'll credit it if you convert to dedicated.
[06:49] Elena: switching back, any blockers for us to publish a listing?
[06:53] Maya: main blockers are: packaging manifest, security artifacts (SOC2/PCI if relevant), and a working test that demonstrates your runtime meets our healthcheck. Once those are in place we can start the marketplace review.
[07:06] Priya: can we discuss KMS — specifically bringing our own HSM via CloudHSM or external HSM provider. Is that supported?
[07:14] Samir: yes for Private we support CloudHSM and can integrate external HSM via PKCS#11 bridges. For hosted, we partner with cloud KMS providers but can arrange a bring-your-own-KMS with appropriate key grants. We'll need to capture the key policies.
[07:31] Tom: note — our initial pilot will be in APAC region; any region-specific constraints?
[07:36] Jordan: we have APAC regions — latency and available instance types vary. We'll run region-specific benchmarks. Also marketplace listing has region tags so you can indicate region availability.
[07:46] Elena: excellent. question — how do rollouts work? If we push a new container image for the marketplace listing, how do you prevent in-flight session breakage?
[07:55] Jordan: good point — we support canary rollouts and session affinity. For streaming sessions we allow sticky routing to the same runtime until session end, and we'll route new sessions to the new image after canary passes. If it's a major model rev we invalidate caches. We'll capture the exact observability signals you want to gate on.
[08:15] Priya: on the agent side, are there any audit logs for who requested what in the runtime? We need an immutable audit trail.
[08:21] Samir: yes audit logs with request_id, user_id, role, and action are available; retention is configurable for enterprise tiers.
[08:30] Maya: okay switching — Jordan will run a quick live demo of a synthetic streaming run from our side, then we can talk specifics for your payload. Jordan?
[08:36] Jordan: sure I'll share my screen — starting a streaming session now, note the first-token latency is ~45ms on this demo node — this is a small model though.
[08:48] (demo noise)
[09:01] Jordan: you can see the KV-cache hit-rate climbing as we feed repeated prefixes, tail lat drops from ~140ms to ~60ms after warmup.
[09:12] Tom: that's promising. Can we capture the raw traces?
[09:15] Jordan: yes will export zip with spans and the token timings.
[09:20] Elena: quick question — for billing and marketplace metering, how do we surface per-route cost?
[09:26] Maya: our billing includes per-token units and a per-embedding metric; we expose per-route breakdowns in the console and via an API. We'll include an example CSV mapping for your marketplace page.
[09:38] Tom: about TLS termination — for private we want TLS to terminate on our side, then mutual TLS to Redwood. Are cert rotations supported?
[09:45] Samir: yes cert rotation is supported; for private we can accept customer-provided certs and we rotate via ACME or scheduled rotation; we'll coordinate with your ops.
[09:56] Priya: one more — can we restrict model variants per customer? Some tenants must avoid experimental weights.
[10:02] Jordan: yes RBAC and model allowlists are supported; you can pin tenants to specific model versions and disallow experimental flags.
[10:12] Elena: cool. I'd like to go over a timeline quickly. We want a pilot in staging, then marketplace listing in production. Our desired timeline: pilot week of Oct 20, UAT week of Oct 27, listing go-live Nov 3. Are those realistic?
[10:26] Maya: yes pilot week of Oct 20 is doable if we get staging creds this week and we run the bench early. We'll aim to have packaging and listing docs to you by Oct 14.
[10:34] Tom: on the staging creds — what exactly do you need?
[10:37] Jordan: VPC peering info, IAM role ARN for the test account, minimal security group openings for the runtime ports, and a sample traffic generator container.
[10:45] Priya: we'll provision a cross-account role and short-lived keys for the test run.
[10:49] (brief pause)
[10:55] Jordan: scoping follow-up — for the benchmark we'll need 3 payload files: typical short convo, typical long convo (~1.2k tokens), and orchestration-level burst file. Please include tokenization ground truth.
[11:12] Tom: we'll export the logs in newline-delimited JSON and include token counts.
[11:17] Maya: perfect. Any blockers or concerns from CascadeForge?
[11:22] Elena: only the typical legal review and KMS policy sign-off. Also let's confirm marketplace fees and revenue share — but that's business, not technical.
[11:33] Maya: we'll loop in partnerships for the fees. Technical is where we close this call.
[11:37] Ravi: one small ask — can you supply a short demo video of the private onboarding steps for our docs team?
[11:42] Maya: yes we'll record a 5–7 minute runbook video for the onboarding steps.
[11:46] Jordan: final note — we'll test both cold and warm cache scenarios and include a recommended autoscaling policy template.
[11:53] Elena: great, recap of owners?
[11:56] Maya: Jordan runs benchmarks; Maya shares packaging + legal stub; Tom provisions staging; Priya collects security artifacts. We'll reconvene after Jordan shares bench results.
[12:10] (end recap)
[12:15] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll post notes and next steps in the shared drive.
[12:20] Elena: thanks all.
[12:22] (meeting ends)
notes: Demo indicated KV-cache can reduce tail latency by ~2x after warmup in synthetic demo
Marketplace listing supports region tags and deployment options metadata
Private deployment supports customer KMS (CloudHSM) and PKCS#11 for external HSMs
